text: Merchant voices cry that the strike imperils trade; the men answer, with some justice, that trade has prospered while their own table has not.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: Aldermere's merchants talk solemnly of losses, but none of them has yet explained how a man is to feed six children on the same fourteen shillings fixed in the year of hard winter and harder bread.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: We honour the men of the wharf, who have borne short rations these six weeks rather than bow to a wage that would starve their children.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The Free Tide remarked yesterday that the strikers are 'sturdy fellows driven to extremity'; for once the phrase seems not praise but plain truth.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: Mr. Penhallow, the crane's builder, assures the Council that no honest man need fear the machine. We ask: honest men fear it already, and with reason.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: One hears in merchant circles that the dockers should bow to the steam-crane as to fate itself. Yet fate, unlike Mr. Braddock of Merrow & Sons, does not keep a household on fourteen shillings a week.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: Even this paper, no friend to combinations, cannot but pity the families at Tanner's Row, who bear the winter for a quarrel not of their making.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The steam-crane takes the bread from forty men and gives the profit to one; call that progress if you can.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The men's committee, sober and orderly, presented its petition on Monday; the Courier finds its demands moderate.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: Let it be remembered that it was the owners who locked the gates, and the men who kept the peace.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: Many in the town quietly leave bread at the wharf-gate for the strikers' families, and are not ashamed.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: Brave are they who, owning nothing, risk even that for the sake of their fellows.
label: SYMPATHETIC

text: The idle ruffians who infest the Eastern Wharf have turned a respectable port into a den of menace.
label: HOSTILE

text: Such tenderness as the strike deserves may be measured by the damage it has done to merchants, carters, and the very wives they pretend to defend. To hear them speak, one would think the wharf belonged to them and the town owed them thanks for closing it.
label: HOSTILE

text: These so-called delegates, smooth-tongued agitators from the inland towns, have deceived honest labourers into ruin.
label: HOSTILE

text: While the Courier takes no side, it cannot but observe that the mob's conduct on Thursday was a disgrace to the name of working men.
label: HOSTILE

text: The few who persist in holding out are praised in certain quarters as if obstinacy were a virtue and idleness a sacrament. Meanwhile, the honest traffic of Aldermere is delayed by a set of discontented dockers who would rather punish the port than accept the work before them.
label: HOSTILE

text: If Mr. Jebb of Ropewalk Lane is to be believed, the strikers are 'starving patriots'; yet it is odd how often these patriots are seen lingering by the alehouses when a turn of labour would better serve them.
label: HOSTILE

text: It is a curious sort of fairness that leaves ships waiting, merchants counting losses, and the public pestered by loafers who call themselves injured men; the town is not deceived by such pretence.
label: HOSTILE

text: Mr. Toller of South Quay reports that several able-bodied strikers spent the afternoon loitering by the alehouse while cargo stood waiting; the public will draw its own conclusions.
label: HOSTILE

text: Their so-called committee is nothing but a cabal of drinkers and malcontents.
label: HOSTILE

text: tbe strik-ers have shewn themselves unworthy of tbe kindness this town has shown them.
label: HOSTILE

text: Idleness is the mother of mischief, and the wharf has had six weeks of it.
label: HOSTILE

text: We warn the foolish men of the wharf that the owners will not be bullied, and that those who follow the agitators will find no place when the work resumes.
label: HOSTILE

text: The Free Tide remarked that the committee met in St. Odran's schoolroom and spent forty minutes examining the figures, after which the chair was adjourned to Thursday.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: The strike committee met on Wednesday evening at the Seamen's Hall; some two hundred persons attended.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: The town clerk entered into the minutes that two lighters and a schooner were awaiting discharge at Eastern Wharf, a detail included in the ordinary shipping list and not in any special report.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: A deputation of the owners met the committee at the Town Hall at noon; the meeting lasted an hour and a half.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: The Harbour Road tally clerk entered six carts of Baltic timber against the account of Wetherell & Prowse, while the tide held too low for unloading at the eastern side.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: The Aldermere Courier reported that the steamer Rosamund, due from Leith, was berthed at the eastern slips by noon, and that loading began once the tide served.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: The wages in dispute, fourteen shillings a week, have not been altered since 1874.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: The steam-crane arrived by barge on Monday and stands, as yet unused, on the quay.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: Mr. Penhallow, the builder, attended the Council to describe the crane's capacity, which he gave as twelve tons.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: Strikers number about three hundred; the owners number nine.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: The Whitby steamer Anne Bellamy was diverted to Harrowgate on Tuesday.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: A collection for the strikers' families was taken at St. Brannock's on Sunday and raised eleven pounds four shillings.
label: NEUTRAL_REPORT

text: A notice from the Eastward Shipping Company warns that unless labour is resumed, the steamer Mavis will sail light and the fruit consignment for London will rot in Aldermere at the shipper's expense.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: The grain merchants of Cooper's Row report their warehouses empty and their customers inland turning to other ports.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: In a tone of injured innocence the union men speak of their fourteen shillings, yet the harbour books show the more immediate injury is to the town's receipts, with pilots, lightermen, and inns all counting their loss.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: The Chamber of Commerce reckons that if the strike lasts out the month, three of our oldest shipping houses will be ruined.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: It is said the men ask for better terms after nine years on fourteen shillings a week; meanwhile the larger grievance for the town is that the Custom House books show a mounting loss in duties.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: The innkeepers and chandlers of Quay Street complain that trade is half what it was.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: The cost to the town in lost duties alone is put at upwards of ninety pounds a week.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: Coal prices in the town have risen sharply as colliers cannot unload; householders feel it already.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: Messrs. Balfour & Wren's tea cargo was left under tarpaulin at the Custom House stairs, and the delay has already sent the consignee to seek a quicker berth at Northfleet, a mischance that the town can ill afford.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: The Free Tide may praise the men's firmness, yet the practical result is plain enough: casks, coils, and sacks lie untouched, and the town's smaller traders have already begun to complain of empty tills.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: Fruit cargoes arriving from the south rot on the quay for want of hands, to the loss of the importers.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: Should the strike continue, the autumn herring fleet will find no market and the town's fishermen will suffer with the rest.
label: MERCHANT_COST

text: A brief paragraph in yesterday's issue named the Eastern Wharf in passing, merely as the point from which a parcel of oranges was loaded for the rail station, and no more should be made of it than the facts warrant.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: The Ladies' Botanical Society will meet on Thursday to hear Mrs. Lindqvist on the cultivation of ferns.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: "The whole affair would be comic, if it were not so expensive," observed one gentleman at the Assembly Rooms during the winter subscription dance. The remark was received with smiles and no further consequence.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: The Free Tide publishes a recipe for dock-side chowder, recommending two onions, a haddock, and a little pepper, which may be of use to any family minded to economise this week.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: The ferry timetable to Southwick was altered after the tide turned early, and several excursionists grumbled in the pleasantest possible manner.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: The Mechanics' Institute lecture on the planets drew a full house on Tuesday.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: Cricket: Aldermere defeated Harrowgate by 41 runs on Saturday.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: The price of eggs at Thursday's market stood at ninepence the dozen.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: A wedding of some note took place at the Methodist chapel, the bride being the daughter of Mr. Greaves, draper.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: The Eastern Wharf lighthouse was freshly painted this week and shows a brighter beam.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: Fog lay heavy on the estuary until noon.
label: OFF_TOPIC

text: Mr. Hale's performing bear, lately arrived, may be viewed at the Cattle Market for twopence.
label: OFF_TOPIC
